# Apple Silicon

### Overview
Apple Silicon is Apple's family of custom ARM-based system-on-chip (SoC) processors designed in-house for Macs, iPads, and iPhones. The lineup spans the A-series (mobile) and M-series (Mac/iPad Pro), integrating CPU, GPU, Neural Engine, and unified memory on a single die. Apple Silicon also powers Apple's Private Cloud Compute servers used for off-device AI workloads.

### Key Ideas & Contributions
- Houses the **16-core Neural Engine**, Apple's dedicated hardware accelerator for on-device machine learning and AI inference
- Foundation for **Apple Intelligence**, enabling most AI workloads to run locally on-device without cloud dependency
- Powers **Private Cloud Compute** — Apple Silicon servers with end-to-end encryption that handle AI tasks too heavy for the user's device
- Central to Apple's "razor-blade" AI strategy: sell premium hardware (the razor), then deliver AI capabilities as the recurring value layer (the blade)
- Chip families referenced in vault: **A18 Pro, A19** (mobile), **M4, M5** (Mac/iPad)

### Related Entities
- **Apple** — designer and manufacturer
- **Neural Engine** — ML accelerator block embedded within Apple Silicon
- **Apple Intelligence** — on-device AI platform built on Apple Silicon capabilities
- **Private Cloud Compute** — server-side AI infrastructure running Apple Silicon
- **Google / Gemini** — partner providing cloud AI models for tasks beyond on-device capacity
